q: How much energy does a hydrogen atom in the ground state need for its electron to move to level $n = 3$ ($E_n = -\tfrac{13.6\,\text{eV}}{n^2}$)?
a: $E_3 - E_1 = -\tfrac{13.6\,\text{eV}}{9} + 13.6\,\text{eV} = 12.1\,\text{eV}$. The photon must bring exactly this energy to be absorbed.

q: Why do the visible-light lines in the hydrogen spectrum come from transitions that end on level $n = 2$?
a: The energies of transitions ending on level $n = 2$ are at most $3.40\,\text{eV}$, and the photons of the four smallest ($1.89$–$3.02\,\text{eV}$) are visible light. The energies of transitions ending in the ground state are over $10\,\text{eV}$ (ultraviolet) and those of transitions ending on level $n = 3$ under $1.51\,\text{eV}$ (infrared).
